text:
**Observations — East Shore, Turn 6**
- Grove of four palm trees, clustered ~8m diameter. Mature, crowns 10-12m high. Fronds green, no dieback visible.
- One fallen trunk, hollow, lying northeast-southwest. Entrance at broken end faces inland; interior ~40cm diameter, 2m deep. No scorch marks, no tool marks, no occupation sign (no ash, fiber, bone).
- Sand shelf continues under grove, firm. No undergrowth, no leaf litter beyond dry fronds.
- Driftwood line ends here — shore curves northeast into mangrove fringe (visible 30m on), impassable without cutting.
- Wind still NE, reduced under canopy. No bird calls, no insect noise.

**Actions**
- Check hollow trunk interior with light — dry sand, two crab casings, nothing artificial.
- Scan trunks for blazes, ropes, carvings. None.
- Note bearing back to driftwood start (265° mag).
- Drink.

**Working hypothesis (guess)**: Palms suggest freshwater lens. Hollow trunk could be emergency shelter or cache point. Mangrove fringe likely rings much of east cove.

**Next**: Return west along driftwood line to south shore start, then continue west unless directed.
